Question
========
You want to compare the distributions of a numeric variable across three groups on the same plot. Why might overlaid
kernel density plots be preferable to overlaid histograms for this purpose?

Answerlist
----------
* Because density plots don't require choosing any smoothing parameter, unlike histograms, which require choosing bins.
* Because density plots draw smooth, continuous curves that can be overlaid without the visual clutter of overlapping bars.
* Because density plots always reveal more detail about the data than histograms do.
* Because density plots ignore differences in sample size between the groups being compared.

Solution
========

Answerlist
----------
* Wrong: density plots still require choosing a smoothing parameter, the bandwidth, which plays a role similar to bin width.
* Correct: continuous curves are easier to visually separate and compare than several sets of overlapping bars.
* Wrong: whether a density plot reveals more or less detail depends on the chosen bandwidth, just as a histogram depends on bin choice.
* Wrong: density plots are still affected by sample size, just like histograms.
